_comment: WHY THIS EXISTS: there is NO built-in policy of any kind for
Microsoft.Fabric. Verified 2026-09-25 - the built-in policy repository has
no Fabric category, and a scoped code search for 'Microsoft.Fabric' across
built-in-policies returns zero results. A custom definition is the only
WHY IT MATTERS HERE: Fabric capacity is exactly the shape of spend this
playbook exists to bound - a single resource, trivially created, billed
hourly on the provisioned tier regardless of use. F64 is the licence
threshold tier and a large step up from F8. An innovation sandbox does not
need it, and nobody should be able to create one by accident.
This is the half of the guardrail that RBAC cannot do. The custom role
grants Microsoft.Fabric write so the team can innovate; this policy is
ALIAS VERIFIED against the live provider:

properties.displayName: Microsoft Fabric capacities must use an approved SKU
properties.description: Denies or audits Microsoft.Fabric capacities created with a SKU outside the approved list. Fabric capacity bills hourly on the provisioned tier regardless of utilisation, so the SKU is the cost decision.

metadata.description: Audit reports without blocking. Deny blocks the deployment.
